Version 2 · reversed loop

Mt Hood → Bend → Oregon Outback → Coast → Olympic → home

Ten days, nine nights, tent camping only, counter-clockwise. Dark skies on nights 3 and 4, the whole Pacific coast on the way back, and Hurricane Ridge on the final morning before the ferry into Seattle.

Sept 4–13, 2026Fri → Sun
~1,565 mifull loop
9 nightsall tent camping
Sept 6 & 7dark-sky nights
5–6 hrsmoonless dark per night

Yes — Sept 4–13 reversed works, and the moon is not a problem

I was worried when you said reverse, because that puts the dark-sky nights at the start of the trip rather than on the Sept 11 new moon. Then I checked moonrise times, and it doesn't matter at all.

Sept 6 and 7 are waning crescents — they rise in the small hours rather than hanging in the evening sky:

NightIllumFull dark fromMoon risesMoonless window
Sun Sept 626.0%9:06 pm2:07 am5h 01m
Mon Sept 716.5%9:04 pm3:26 am6h 22m

Five to six hours of completely moonless sky each night, starting the moment it gets dark. And the Milky Way core sets around midnight in September anyway — so a moon that doesn't show up until 2 am costs you nothing at all. You get the good half of the night twice.

Three ways reversing actually improves the trip

1. The charging risk inverts in your favour. This is the big one. Going clockwise you arrived at Summer Lake after a 210-mile run with ~25% left and no fallback. Counter-clockwise you arrive from Bend after only 125 miles at around 60% — so even if the campground's 240V pedestal is dead, you can simply drive back to Bend. Then you charge two full nights and leave near 100% for the 210 miles to Eugene. Same roads, far more margin.

2. You spend Labor Day weekend inland. Sept 5–7 is the holiday. Lake County is empty; the Olympic Peninsula is not. The old plan had you fighting for first-come sites at Heart O' the Hills on the busiest Saturday of the season. Now the coast and Olympic fall midweek and after.

3. It ends properly. Hurricane Ridge on the last morning, then the Kingston ferry into Seattle — rather than a 600-mile I-84 slog home. You also gain Mt Hood and Smith Rock, which the old route missed entirely.

What it costs you

Sept 8 is a 270-mile day — Summer Lake over Willamette Pass to the coast at Florence. It's the price of putting the desert and the ocean in the same trip; there's no way around it in either direction.

Kalaloch on Sept 11 is still inside its reservation season (which runs to Sept 20), so that hasn't changed. And you're still inside the 6-month booking window, so first-come-first-served sites remain the backbone of the plan.

The route

Camp for the night Tesla Supercharger Stop / sight Charging gap warning Outbound — Seattle → Outback Return — coast & Olympic Dark Sky Sanctuary

Counter-clockwise: amber out through Mt Hood and Bend, blue back up the coast and around the peninsula. Screenshot it before you lose signal.

Day-by-day

1Fri 9/4
Seattle → Mt HoodI-5 → Portland → US-26 → Trillium Lake
230 miPortland + Sandy›
Route

I-5 south through Olympia and Centralia → Portland → US-26 east over Mt Hood → Government Camp → Trillium Lake, 2 mi off the highway.

Straightforward interstate for the first four hours, then it gets good the moment you turn onto US-26. Leave early — you want to be setting up before dark on a Friday of a holiday weekend.

Charging

SuperchargerPortland — Jantzen Beach, 12154 N Pavilion Ave. 8 stalls, up to 250 kW — the fastest charge of the entire trip. Take a proper break here.

SuperchargerSandy, OR — Fred Meyer lot, right on US-26. Last easy charge before the mountain; top to 90% if you plan to explore around Hood.

Centralia, WA is a useful mid-morning splash on I-5 if you leave with less than a full battery.

Camp

Trillium Lake Campground, Mt Hood NF, 3,600 ft. The postcard reflection of Mt Hood across the lake is genuinely as good as the photos, and it's a 2-mile flat loop around the shore.

$26/site + $8 vehicle fee. Most sites are reservable on recreation.gov, but sites 58–64 near the dam are walk-in tent-only and first-come-first-served — that's your realistic play this late. Drinking water and vault toilets on site.

Backup 1 Still Creek Campground, 1 mi away
Backup 2 Ainsworth or Viento State Park in the Columbia Gorge, if you'd rather run I-84

2Sat 9/5
Mt Hood → Central OregonWarm Springs · Smith Rock · Bend
135 miBend SC›
Route

US-26 southeast down the east flank of the Cascades through the Warm Springs reservation to Madras, then US-97 to Terrebonne and Bend. Short driving day by design — the landscape flips from wet fir forest to juniper and sage within an hour, which is the whole point.

Smith Rock State Park is the stop: 600 ft of welded tuff above the Crooked River, the Misery Ridge loop (3.7 mi, genuinely steep), and one of the birthplaces of American sport climbing.

Charging

SuperchargerBend — 61535 S Hwy 97, 8 stalls, 150 kW, 24/7.

This is the last certain fast charge before Lake County. Charge to 100% either tonight or first thing tomorrow morning. Central Oregon has additional Superchargers around Madras and Redmond — worth confirming on the app, but Bend is the one to plan around.

Camp

Tumalo State Park, on the Deschutes just north of Bend — reservable, showers, and close enough to town to resupply properly before the desert.

Backup 1 Smith Rock bivouac — walk-in tent-only, first-come-first-served, very cheap. Basic (no fires) but you wake up under the rock
Backup 2 LaPine State Park, 30 mi south — puts you closer to tomorrow's turn

Do your full resupply in Bend: food for three days, 5–7 gallons of water, firewood, fuel. Paisley has a saloon and a small store, and that is it.
3Sun 9/6
Into the Oregon OutbackOutback Scenic Byway · Fort Rock · Summer Lake
125 miL2 overnight🌒 26% · dark 5h›
Route

US-97 south to La Pine, then OR-31 — the Outback Scenic Byway — southeast through Silver Lake and Summer Lake to the hot springs, 6 mi west of Paisley. Only 125 miles, and it feels like leaving the country.

Stop at Fort Rock State Natural Area, 7 mi off OR-31: a 300 ft volcanic tuff ring standing alone in flat desert, formed when magma met the floor of a Pleistocene lake. Sandals woven ~10,000 years ago were found in the cave nearby.

Charging

Leave Bend at 100%. 125 miles gets you to Summer Lake at roughly 55–60% in your Extended Range truck — which is the safety margin the reversed route buys you. If the campground's 240V pedestal turns out to be dead, you can still drive back to Bend on what's in the battery.

After La Pine there is no DC fast charging. The only public charger in all of Lake County is a Level 2 at Santa's Hardware in Christmas Valley — $2/hr, 9–5, business days.

Camp

Summer Lake Hot Springs — OR-31, 6 mi west of Paisley. (541) 943-3931. Two nights.

  • ~12 tent sites plus a 5-acre dry camping field. $20 per person per night. Open flat ground, fire pits, no tables, no trees
  • Book a 20–50 amp full-hookup site (+$20/night) and tent on it. Plug in the Ford Mobile Power Cord: ~7.7 kW, ~17 miles of range per hour, so each 12-hour night puts roughly 200 miles back in the truck. Two nights and you leave full
  • Geothermal soaking pools on site — and after a day in the high desert, exactly what you want

Free alternative Summer Lake Wildlife Area — four primitive ODFW campgrounds. Free to camp with a $10/day ODFW permit that is not sold on site — buy it online first. Tables, fire pits, vault toilets, no water, no power. Darker than the hot springs; use it for the viewing session and sleep where the outlet is.

Tonight

Sunset 7:32 pm · full astronomical darkness 9:06 pm · moon doesn't rise until 2:07 am.

That's five straight hours of moonless sky, and the Milky Way core is up in the southwest for all of it. Use tonight to scout a spot on the wildlife area auto tour route and get the camera dialled in — tomorrow is the better night and you want the fumbling done.

4Mon 9/7
Oregon Outback Dark Sky SanctuaryThe night the trip is built around
~110 mi localL2 overnight🌒 16.5% · dark 6h22m›
The place

Certified by DarkSky International in March 2024, the Oregon Outback International Dark Sky Sanctuary covers 2.5 million acres of Lake County — the largest dark sky sanctuary in the world. On a clear night you can see roughly 15,000 stars, against about 500 from a typical city.

Daytime
  • Summer Lake Wildlife Area auto tour route — 8,800 acres of marsh under the 3,000 ft Winter Ridge escarpment. Big birding, and the best viewing ground for tonight
  • Paisley — the Pioneer Saloon, one of the oldest bars in Oregon. Something that isn't camp food
  • Chewaucan River south of Paisley — swimming holes and Marster Spring
  • Keep the driving light. A long soak in the pools and an afternoon nap is the correct strategy before an all-night session
Carry a paper map. Cell coverage across Lake County is unreliable to nonexistent, and this is not terrain to improvise in after dark. Download offline maps too, and tell someone your plan.
The night
Sunset7:30 pm PDT
Astronomical dark9:04 pm PDT
Moonrise3:26 am — a thin 16.5% crescent, low in the east
Moonless window6 hours 22 minutes, 9:04 pm → 3:26 am
Milky Way coreSouthwest at full dark, setting toward midnight — shoot it first
After midnightAndromeda, Perseus and the Double Cluster climbing in the northeast

Practical: red light only, and give your eyes a full 30 minutes. Elevation ~4,200 ft — expect 30s to low 40s °F overnight. You're on shore power, so run a dew heater and an electric blanket all night for free.

5Tue 9/8
Desert → oceanThe long one. Willamette Pass to the dunes.
270 miEugene SC›
Route

OR-31 back north to La Pine → US-97 → OR-58 over Willamette Pass (5,128 ft), past Odell and Crescent Lakes → down the Middle Fork Willamette to Eugene → OR-126 along the Siuslaw to Florence.

Stretch stop: Salt Creek Falls off OR-58 — 286 ft, second tallest in Oregon, and a two-minute walk from the parking area.

High desert at breakfast, Pacific surf at dinner. It's a long day but it's the single most dramatic transition on the trip.

Charging

You leave Summer Lake essentially full after two nights on the 240V — which is why this direction is the safer one. Summer Lake → Eugene is 210 mi with a 4,700 ft climb; expect to arrive around 25–30%.

SuperchargerEugene — first fast charge in three days. Then it's only 60 mi to Florence.

Bail-out: if something has gone wrong and you're low leaving Summer Lake, turn north at La Pine for the Bend Supercharger (30 mi) rather than committing to Willamette Pass.

ODOT has NEVI-funded fast chargers planned for Chemult and Klamath Falls. If the Chemult site is live by September it sits right on US-97 and removes this leg's only real pinch point. Check PlugShare the morning of.
Camp

Jessie M. Honeyman Memorial State Park, 3 mi south of Florence — dunes, two freshwater lakes, 350+ sites with a large tent loop.

Backup 1 Carl G. Washburne State Park, north of Florence
Backup 2 Tugman State Park, 20 mi south

Sand stakes for this one and for Fort Stevens — standard tent stakes don't hold in dune sand.
6Wed 9/9
Central coast, northboundHeceta Head · Cape Perpetua · Newport · Depoe Bay
130 miLincoln City SC›
Route

US-101 north, and northbound is the better direction on this coast — you're on the ocean side of the road all day, so every pullout is a right turn.

  • Heceta Head lighthouse and the Sea Lion Caves, 12 mi up
  • Cape Perpetua — Thor's Well and Devil's Churn. Go near high tide or don't bother
  • Yachats, then Yaquina Bay into Newport — Yaquina Head lighthouse, historic bayfront
  • Depoe Bay — smallest navigable harbour in the world, and September is peak gray whale season
Charging

SuperchargerLincoln City — 1500 SE East Devils Lake Rd, 8 stalls, 150 kW, 24/7. The one solid fast charge on the coast run; take it to 90%.

Florence has Level 2 destination chargers only, so don't count on topping up before you leave.

Camp

Cape Lookout State Park, south of Tillamook — a sand spit between the ocean and Netarts Bay, with a proper tent loop back in the trees.

Backup 1 Beverly Beach State Park, just north of Newport
Backup 2 Nehalem Bay State Park, further north — shortens tomorrow

7Thu 9/10
North coast → Columbia mouthTillamook · Cannon Beach · Astoria
90 miSeaside SC›
Route

Short day — use the time. Tillamook creamery, then Cannon Beach for Haystack Rock (check the tide table; low tide opens the pools), Ecola State Park for the classic headland view, and into Astoria.

The Astoria Column is worth the 164 steps for the view over the Columbia mouth and out to the bar.

Charging

SuperchargerSeaside — Seaside Outlet Mall, 1111 N Roosevelt Dr, 8 stalls. Astoria itself has no Supercharger, so charge at Seaside on the way past. Tillamook has other-network DC fast charging as a fallback.

Camp

Fort Stevens State Park, Hammond — 470+ sites, the wreck of the Peter Iredale on the beach, and old coastal artillery batteries to poke around. Biggest campground on the trip and your best odds of finding something late.

Backup Cape Disappointment State Park on the Washington side — two lighthouses and the Lewis & Clark centre. Needs a WA Discover Pass.

8Fri 9/11
Into Washington → Olympic coastMegler Bridge · Aberdeen · Kalaloch
175 miAberdeen SC›
Route

The 4.1-mile Astoria–Megler Bridge across the Columbia, then US-101 north through Raymond and the Willapa lowlands to Aberdeen, up past Lake Quinault and into Olympic National Park.

Arrive at Ruby Beach for golden hour — sea stacks, bleached driftwood, and usually a bank of fog doing something interesting offshore.

Charging

SuperchargerAberdeen — 416 E Wishkah St. After the Chehalis River bridge go straight rather than turning left, then first right and right again.

Charge to 90–100% here. Aberdeen to Forks is ~150 mi with nothing in between, and tomorrow includes the Hoh detour.

Camp

Kalaloch Campground — on the bluff directly above the Pacific. Reservable through Sept 20, and sites release in three staggered blocks by loop: 6 months, 2 weeks, and 4 days ahead. The 4-day release on Sept 7 is your realistic shot — set an alarm for it.

Backup 1 South Beach Campground, just south — FCFS
Backup 2 Bogachiel State Park, 6 mi south of Forks (Discover Pass)

Everything scented goes in the truck bed tonight. Olympic requires hard-sided storage for food, toothpaste, sunscreen and chapstick — and the raccoons on this stretch of coast are professionals. Your Retrax is exactly the right tool.
9Sat 9/12
Hoh Rain Forest → Lake CrescentThe wettest and greenest day
150 miForks SC›
Route

North on 101, then Upper Hoh Road 18 mi in to the Hoh Rain Forest — Hall of Mosses (0.8 mi) and the Spruce Nature Trail (1.2 mi). Back out to Forks, then north and east to Lake Crescent.

If you have appetite: Rialto Beach and Hole-in-the-Wall, 14 mi off 101 at Forks. Or Sol Duc Falls, 1.6 mi round trip, on the way to camp.

Charging

SuperchargerForks — 100 Fern Hill Rd. Charge here before or after the Hoh; the detour is 36 mi round trip with no charging and no cell service, and there's nothing again until Sequim.

Camp

Fairholme — west end of Lake Crescent, 88 sites, first-come-first-served, right on the water. Glacially carved, 600 ft deep, and an unreasonable shade of blue.

Backup Sol Duc Campground — reservable, and it puts you next to the hot springs pools if you'd rather end soft

10Sun 9/13
Hurricane Ridge → ferry homeBest possible last morning
150 miSequim SC›
Route

Marymere Falls (1.8 mi round trip) from Lake Crescent first thing, then east to Port Angeles and 17 miles up Hurricane Ridge Road to 5,242 ft. On a clear morning you're looking straight across at the Bailey Range and Mount Olympus, with the Strait of Juan de Fuca and Vancouver Island behind you.

Down, east through Sequim, then WA-104 to the Kingston–Edmonds ferry and home.

Hurricane Ridge is open in summer 2026 but expect road and meadow trail construction, and there are no indoor facilities — the lodge burned in 2023, so it's temporary trailers and vault toilets. Check the NPS road status page before you drive up. The regen on the way down gives back a good share of the climb.
Charging

SuperchargerSequim — Holiday Inn Express, 1441 W Washington St, 8 stalls, 150 kW, 24/7. Only Supercharger on the north peninsula and all you need to get home.

Book the ferry. Sunday afternoon sailings out of Kingston fill up; without a vehicle reservation you can wait through two or three boats.

What changed from V1

Gained

  • Mt Hood and Trillium Lake — a real first night instead of an interstate slog
  • Smith Rock and Central Oregon
  • Hurricane Ridge as the finale, with a ferry home rather than 600 miles of I-84
  • An extra night — 9 instead of 7
  • Charging margin at Summer Lake — arrive at 60%, not 25%
  • Labor Day spent inland, where nobody is

Lost or unchanged

  • The Sept 11 new moon exactly — but the waning crescent gives you 5–6 moonless hours anyway, so this is on paper only
  • Sept 8 is still a 270-mile day
  • Still inside the 6-month booking window, so FCFS sites remain the backbone
  • Wildfire smoke risk is identical, and still the biggest threat to the stargazing
  • Southern coast below Florence (Bandon, Coos Bay) — was never in the plan

Book this week

  • Summer Lake Hot Springs, (541) 943-3931 — hookup site, Sept 6 and 7, and confirm the pedestal amperage. Do this one first; everything else has alternatives
  • Kingston–Edmonds ferry, Sunday Sept 13 afternoon
  • ODFW parking permit — $10/day or $30/yr, online. Not sold at the wildlife area
  • Ford NACS adapter and a NEMA 14-50 for the Mobile Power Cord — the trip does not work without either
  • Crossbars, if you decide to bring the cargo basket at all — see the gear notes in V1
  • Cancellation alerts on recreation.gov for Trillium Lake, Kalaloch (Sept 11) and Sol Duc; and Oregon State Parks for Tumalo, Honeyman, Cape Lookout and Fort Stevens
V2, built Aug 1 2026. Moon phases, moonrise and astronomical twilight computed for 42.74°N, 120.63°W (Summer Lake Hot Springs), elev. 1,265 m, in PDT. Charger locations, campground reservation windows and road status should be re-verified close to departure. Gear, weather and packing notes are in the V1 document and still apply — only the dates and direction have changed.
